mainTopic: When a debtor's claim "פרעתי" is believed, when he becomes a כפרן, and when a found שטר חוב is returned.
overview: The amud opens with a debate about a borrower who says "פרעתי" (I paid) after בית דין ruled against him. One view splits the court's wording "צא תן לו" from "חייב אתה ליתן לו". רב זביד says he is believed after either wording. For רב זביד, the wording matters only when witnesses disprove his first "פרעתי" and he says it again: after "צא תן לו" he becomes a כפרן for that money, but after "חייב אתה ליתן לו" he was only stalling. רבי יוחנן adds two more cases of כפרן. The first is someone who denies a loan completely and then claims he paid, backed up by the story of שבתאי and the woolen cloak. The second is someone who falsely claims he took an oath that בית דין required of him. The גמרא then turns to a found שטר חוב with a הנפק dated that same day, which רבי יוחנן says is returned. The גמרא defends this ruling with two explanations: same-day repayment is uncommon, and רב כהנא's case where the borrower admits the debt. The amud ends as רבי יוחנן begins a new teaching about claiming payment after a מעשה בית דין, and the ruling comes on the next amud.

steps.title: After 'Go pay him,' the borrower is believed
steps.stepSummary: The first opinion finishes its first case. If בית דין told the borrower "צא תן לו" and he later says "פרעתי," he is believed, so בית דין does not write a collection document for the lender.
steps.simpleTranslation: …and he said, "I paid," he is believed. If the lender comes to have a document written, they do not write it and give it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining in the middle of a ruling. In the case where בית דין told the borrower "צא תן לו" (go pay him), his later claim "פרעתי" is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "צא תן לו" is a full, final order to pay. Once it is given, it is believable that the borrower went and paid. So the lender cannot get בית דין to write him a document for collecting from the borrower's property.

keyTerms.meaning: "I paid" — the borrower's claim that he already paid the debt
Believed; his claim is accepted
The lender
They write a document and give it to him (a court paper letting the lender collect)

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence starts in the middle. The case being described here is the one where בית דין said "צא תן לו" (go pay him), which was mentioned just before this text begins.

phrases.english: and he said "I paid" — he is believed.
phrases.notes: This picks up the case from just before: בית דין told the borrower "צא תן לו" (go pay him).

phrases.english: If the lender comes to have a document written —
they do not write it and give it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר פָּרַעְתִּי נֶאֱמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ruling that started before this text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the court says "צא תן לו," the borrower's "פרעתי" is believed, and no collection document is written for the lender.

steps.title: After 'You are obligated to pay,' the borrower is not believed
steps.stepSummary: The same opinion's second case. If בית דין only said "חייב אתה ליתן לו," the borrower's "פרעתי" is not believed, and בית דין does write the lender a collection document.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they said, "You are obligated to give him," and he said, "I paid," he is not believed. If the lender comes to have a document written, they write it and give it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: Now comes the opposite case. בית דין only declared that the borrower owes the money ("חייב אתה ליתן לו") but did not order him to go pay. Here his claim "פרעתי" is not believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower did not pay without a court case. So we assume he plans to wait until בית דין gives a final order, and his claim to have paid now is suspect. That is why the lender gets the document to collect.

keyTerms.meaning: "You are obligated to give him" — a ruling that he owes, without a final order to pay
"Go give him" — a final order to go pay
He is not believed

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the contrast between the two court phrases. רב זביד will reject this difference in the next step.

phrases.english: If they said, "You are obligated to give him"
and he said "I paid" — he is not believed.
If the lender comes to have a document written —
they write it and give it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּיב אַתָּה לִיתֵּן לוֹ וְאָמַר פָּרַעְתִּי אֵינוֹ נֶאֱמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite case to step 1, within the same opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the court says "חייב אתה ליתן לו," the borrower's "פרעתי" is not believed, and a collection document is written for the lender.

steps.title: רב זביד: the borrower is believed in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד, quoting רב נחמן, disagrees with the first opinion. Whether בית דין said "צא תן לו" or "חייב אתה ליתן לו," the borrower who says "פרעתי" is believed, and no document is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said in the name of רב נחמן: Whether they said "Go give him" or "You are obligated to give him," if he said "I paid," he is believed. If the lender comes to have a document written, they do not write it and give it to him.
steps.whatsHappening: A second version of the ruling is given. רב זביד says the wording בית דין used makes no difference: in both cases the borrower is believed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion split the two court phrases. רב זביד removes that split. He takes the lenient ruling of the "צא תן לו" case and applies it to the "חייב אתה ליתן לו" case too.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
Whether... or... (both cases are the same)

phrases.aramaic: רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rav Zevid said in the name of Rav Nachman:
Whether they said "Go give him,"
or "You are obligated to give him,"
and he said "I paid" — he is believed.
If the lender comes to have a document written —
they do not write it and give it to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב זְבִיד מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן אָמַר בֵּין צֵא תֵּן לוֹ בֵּין חַיָּיב אַתָּה לִיתֵּן לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the split made in steps 1–2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In both cases ("צא תן לו" and "חייב אתה ליתן לו"), the borrower's "פרעתי" is believed, and no collection document is written.

steps.title: The real difference: proven false once, then claiming again
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד explains when there is a difference. The borrower was told "צא תן לו" and said "פרעתי." Witnesses then testified that he had not paid. If he says "פרעתי" again, he is considered a כפרן for that money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if there is a difference to make, this is the difference: they told him "Go give him," and he said "I paid," and witnesses testify that he did not pay, and then he again said "I paid" — he is established as a denier regarding that money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד continues his statement. He says the wording of the court is not what matters. What matters is whether the borrower was already caught lying about this same debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The borrower already claimed "פרעתי," and witnesses proved it false. So when he says "פרעתי" again, he is not believed. He now has the status of a כפרן (a denier), but only for this particular money ("לאותו ממון").

keyTerms.meaning: If there is a difference to make
And he again said
He is established as a denier (a liar about his debt)
With regard to that same money only

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב זביד, a plain "פרעתי" is believed after either court wording. The wording matters only when witnesses proved his first "פרעתי" false and he says "פרעתי" again. After "צא תן לו" he then becomes a כפרן for that money. After "חייב אתה ליתן לו" he does not (next step).
steps.confusionAlert: The borrower is not called a כפרן just because he said "פרעתי" after the court ruling. It takes a false claim proven by witnesses, followed by the same claim again.
steps.whyThisMatters: This creates the idea of הוחזק כפרן. That status is limited to one specific debt (לאותו ממון). It is not a general loss of trust.

phrases.english: Rather, if there is a difference to make —
this is where there is a difference:
they told him, "Go give him,"
and he said, "I paid,"
and the witnesses testify about him that he did not pay it,
and then he again said, "I paid" —
he is established as a denier regarding that money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אִיכָּא לְפַלּוֹגֵי הָכִי הוּא דְּאִיכָּא לְפַלּוֹגֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב זביד continues his own statement. Having rejected the split in steps 1–2, he gives the one real exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A borrower whose "פרעתי" was disproven by witnesses, and who then says "פרעתי" again, is a כפרן for that money and is not believed.

steps.title: After 'You are obligated to pay' he is not branded a denier
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד gives the opposite case. If בית דין only said "חייב אתה ליתן לו," and the borrower falsely said "פרעתי" and was contradicted by witnesses, saying "פרעתי" again does not make him a כפרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if בית דין said "You are obligated to give him," and he said "I paid," and witnesses testified that he did not pay, and then he said "I paid" again, he is not presumed to be a denier regarding that money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד finishes his point by giving the other half of the contrast. With the softer court statement "חייב אתה ליתן לו," the borrower is not branded a כפרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything in the case is the same as step 4 except the court's wording. In step 4 the court gave a final order, "צא תן לו." Here it only said "you are obligated." That one difference changes the outcome: now his first false "פרעתי" does not ruin his later claim.

keyTerms.meaning: "You are obligated to give him". The court states the law but has not yet given a final order to pay.
He is presumed to be a denier, someone whose claims about this debt are no longer trusted.
Regarding that specific money only, not all his dealings.

steps.confusionAlert: Only the court's wording differs between step 4 and this step. The borrower's behavior is exactly the same in both cases.

phrases.english: But if the court said: "You are obligated to give him"
and he said: "I paid"
and the witnesses testify about him that he did not pay
and he then said again: "I paid"
he is not presumed to be a denier regarding that money.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַיָּיב אַתָּה לִיתֵּן לוֹ וְאָמַר פָּרַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב זביד's contrast begun in step 4 by giving the opposite outcome for the softer court wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After only "חייב אתה ליתן לו," a borrower caught falsely claiming payment does not become a כפרן for that money.

steps.title: Why is he not considered a denier?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 5.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why this borrower is not branded a liar, since witnesses showed he did not pay. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is fair. He said something false in front of witnesses, just like the borrower in step 4. The גמרא needs to explain why that lie counts against him there but not here.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the logic behind step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a borrower who falsely said "פרעתי" after "חייב אתה ליתן לו" is not treated as a כפרן.

steps.title: He was only stalling until the court reviewed his case
steps.stepSummary: The borrower was not really denying the debt. He was putting the lender off, thinking the court had not finished with his case yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: He was just trying to slip away from him for now. He thought: "Until the rabbis look into my case again."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the borrower's false "I paid" was a stalling move, not a real denial of the debt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "חייב אתה ליתן לו" sounds like the case is not finished yet. So the borrower felt he could delay paying until the judges looked at it more. A delay like that is not a true lie about the debt, so he does not lose his credibility. After the final order "צא תן לו" there is nothing left to wait for, so a false "I paid" is a real denial.

keyTerms.meaning: To slip away, to evade or push someone off for now.
That they will examine or look into.
The rabbis, here meaning the judges of the court.

steps.whatToRemember: "צא תן לו" is a final order, so a later false "פרעתי" makes him a כפרן. "חייב אתה ליתן לו" is not final, so a false "פרעתי" is only stalling and he is not a כפרן.

phrases.english: he was just evading him

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר עַד דִּמְעַיְּינוּ בִּי רַבָּנַן בְּדִינִי.
phrases.english: thinking: until the rabbis look into my case.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשְׁתְּמוֹטֵי הוּא קָא מִשְׁתְּמִיט מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since the court had not given a final order, his false claim was a delaying tactic and not a real denial.

steps.title: Denying the loan, then claiming to have paid, makes him a denier
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן: if someone denies owing anything, witnesses prove the loan, and he then says "I paid," he is a כפרן for that money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: One says, "I have a מנה in your hand," and the other says, "You have nothing in my hand." Witnesses testify that he does owe it, and he then says, "I paid." He is presumed to be a denier regarding that money.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching from רבי יוחנן: a borrower who first denies the loan entirely, and switches to "I paid" once witnesses prove it, is branded a כפרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no court order at all. The problem is that his two claims contradict each other. "You have nothing of mine" means there never was a loan. "I paid" admits there was a loan. Once witnesses proved his first claim false, his new story is not trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of one hundred זוז (silver coins).
The other one, meaning the defendant.
"You have nothing in my hand," a complete denial of any debt.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
If one says: "I have a maneh in your hand"
and the other says: "You have nothing in my hand"
phrases.notes: He isn't saying "I paid." He is saying there was never any loan at all.

phrases.english: and the witnesses testify about him that he does owe it
and he then turned around and said: "I paid"
he is presumed to be a denier regarding that money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a related case of כפרן that does not involve a court ruling, where the borrower contradicts himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who denies a debt completely, is proven wrong by witnesses, and then claims payment is a כפרן for that money.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a second way to become a כפרן: switching from "there was never a loan" to "I paid it."

steps.title: The story of שבתאי and the woolen cloak
steps.stepSummary: שבתאי son of רבי מרינוס promised his daughter-in-law a fine woolen cloak in her כתובה. When the כתובה was lost, he denied ever writing it. Witnesses proved he did, and he then said "I paid it." רבי חייא ruled that he is a כפרן for that cloak.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this case: שבתאי son of רבי מרינוס wrote for his daughter-in-law a cloak of fine wool in her כתובה, and he took responsibility for it. Her כתובה was lost. He said to her, "These things never happened." Witnesses came and said, "Yes, he wrote it for her." In the end he said to them, "I paid it." He came before רבי חייא, who said to him, "You are presumed to be a denier regarding that cloak."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי יוחנן's rule with a real case. It has the same pattern: a full denial, then witnesses, then "I paid."
steps.deeperAnalysis: שבתאי first said the promise never existed. Witnesses proved it did. Then he switched to "I already gave it." רבי חייא would not accept the new claim and called him a כפרן for that cloak, just as רבי יוחנן ruled.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloak of fine wool.
His daughter-in-law.
Was lost.
"These things never happened," a complete denial.

steps.whatToRemember: Saying "it never happened" and then "I paid," after witnesses prove the debt, makes a person a כפרן for that item. רבי חייא ruled this way in the case of שבתאי.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּשַׁבְּתַאי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מָרִינוּס
phrases.english: Like this case of Shabbetai son of Rabbi Marinus
who wrote for his daughter-in-law
a cloak of fine wool in her כתובה
and he took it upon himself.
phrases.notes: He personally took responsibility for giving her this cloak.

phrases.english: Her כתובה was lost.
He said to her: "These things never happened."

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ סָהֲדֵי וְאָמְרִי: אִין כְּתַב לַהּ.
phrases.english: Witnesses came and said: Yes, he wrote it for her.
In the end he said to them: "I paid it."
The case came before Rabbi Ḥiyya

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הוּחְזַקְתָּ כַּפְרָן לְאוֹתָהּ אִיצְטְלָא.
phrases.english: who said to him: You are presumed to be a denier regarding that cloak.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּשַׁבְּתַאי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי מָרִינוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates and supports רבי יוחנן's rule from step 8 with a case decided by רבי חייא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's rule that denying a debt and then claiming payment makes one a כפרן.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי חייא's ruling in the case of שבתאי son of רבי מרינוס and the woolen cloak.

steps.title: Caught lying about an oath makes him a כפרן for that oath
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if someone owed an oath, claimed he took it, witnesses said he did not, and he repeated that he swore, he becomes a כפרן regarding that oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אלעא, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A man owed his friend an oath. He said, "I already swore." Witnesses testified that he did not swear. He then said again, "I swore." He is treated as a liar regarding that oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling that follows the pattern of steps 8-9, but now about an oath instead of money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 8-9 a person who was proven wrong and then made a new claim became a כפרן for the money. Here the same idea is applied to an oath: once witnesses disprove his claim that he swore, repeating that claim is not believed.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath
"I already swore"
He is established as a denier, a liar who is not believed
Witnesses

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the כפרן status applies to an oath he owed, not only to money: his repeated claim "נשבעתי" about that oath is no longer believed.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said that Rabbi Ela said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
If one owed his fellow an oath,
and he said, "I swore,"
and the witnesses testify about him that he did not swear,
and he again said, "I swore" –
he is established as a denier regarding that oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the כפרן idea from steps 8-9 to someone who owed an oath
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who falsely claims he swore, is contradicted by witnesses, and repeats the claim is a כפרן for that oath.

steps.title: רבי אבהו limits the ruling to an oath imposed by בית דין
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the ruling makes sense only when בית דין required the oath. If the man offered to swear on his own, he is believed, because people often say they will swear and then don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: They told this ruling to רבי אבהו. He said: רבי אבין's ruling makes sense when בית דין obligated him to swear. But if he obligated himself to swear, he is believed. People often say casually that they will swear.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו hears the ruling from step 10 and adds a limit on when it applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When בית דין requires an oath, the person knows it is serious, so claiming falsely that he swore shows real lying. When he only offered to swear on his own, it may have been loose talk. So saying "I swore" afterward does not prove he is a liar.

keyTerms.meaning: It is reasonable, it makes sense
Court
He obligated himself, on his own
Believed, trusted
A person tends to say things casually

phrases.english: They said it before Rabbi Abbahu,
he said to them:
Rabbi Avin's statement is reasonable
where he was obligated to take an oath in court,
but if he obligated himself to take an oath – [he is believed].
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

phrases.english: A person tends to just say it casually.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמְרוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows step 10 to an oath required by בית דין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כפרן rule applies only to an oath imposed by בית דין; if he offered the oath on his own, he is believed.

steps.title: רבי אבין agrees that he meant an oath from בית דין
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אבהו's limit was brought back to רבי אבין, he said that he too was talking about an oath required by בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They brought it back to רבי אבין. He said to them: I also said this about an oath in בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבין answers that רבי אבהו's limit is exactly what he meant all along.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no disagreement. רבי אבין's ruling in step 10 was always about an oath that בית דין required.

keyTerms.meaning: They brought it back
I also

phrases.english: They brought it back before Rabbi Avin,
he said to them:
I too said it about a case in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַהְדְּרוּהָ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אבין accepts רבי אבהו's limit from step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבי אבין mean his ruling to include an oath a person offered on his own?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No; he meant only an oath required by בית דין.

steps.title: Another version of the teaching says בית דין openly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a second version of רבי אבין's teaching that includes the words "in court," confirming the limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אלעא, who said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A man owed his friend an oath in court. He said, "I swore." Witnesses testified that he did not swear. He again said, "I swore." He is treated as a liar regarding that oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports steps 11-12 by quoting a version of the ruling that says "in court" outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This repeats step 10 almost word for word, with one added phrase: בבית דין. That word proves the ruling was always limited to an oath required by בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught

steps.whatToRemember: A person becomes a כפרן for an oath only if בית דין required it and he was caught falsely saying he swore. An oath he offered on his own does not count.
steps.confusionAlert: This step is not just repeating step 10. The only new thing is the word בבית דין, and that is the whole point.

phrases.english: It was also stated:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִלְעָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin said that Rabbi Ela said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה חַיָּיב לַחֲבֵירוֹ שְׁבוּעָה בְּבֵית דִּין
phrases.english: If one owed his fellow an oath in court
and he said, "I swore,"
and the witnesses testify about him that he did not swear,
and he again said, "I swore" –
he is established as a denier regarding that oath.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רבי אבין's answer in step 12 with a version that says בבית דין
steps.raayaObject: That the ruling of step 10 applies only to an oath required by בית דין
steps.raayaSupportSource: A second version of רבי אבין's teaching that includes the word בבית דין

steps.title: A found שטר חוב with a הנפק dated that day goes back to the lender
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that if someone finds a שטר חוב in the market that has a הנפק and is dated that same day, he must return it to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: If someone finds a loan document in the marketplace, and it has a court's approval written on it, and its date is that very day, he should return it to the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic about returning a lost שטר חוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one does not simply return a found שטר חוב, because the loan may already have been paid. Here the note was already approved by בית דין through a הנפק and is dated that same day. In that case רבי יוחנן says to return it to the lender. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: A loan document
A court's approval written on the document
Its date is that same day
He should return it to the owner

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
One who finds a loan document in the marketplace,
and a court approval is written on it,
and its date written on it is that same day –
he should return it to the owner.
phrases.notes: The owner here is the lender, who holds the loan document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about returning found loan documents
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A found שטר חוב with a הנפק, dated the same day, is returned to the lender.

steps.title: Why the found note is returned: two worries removed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן's ruling. The הנפק removes the worry that the loan never happened, and same-day repayment is not a real worry.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you worry that he wrote the note planning to borrow but never borrowed, that can't be, because a הנפק is written in it. If you worry that the loan was repaid, we don't worry about repayment on the same day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the finder of this note should return it. It goes through the two usual worries about a lost note and shows that neither one applies here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a lost note is not returned. Maybe the borrower wrote it but never took the loan, or maybe he already paid. The הנפק proves the lender already brought the note to court, so the loan was real. Since the note is dated today, we assume nobody pays back a loan on the same day he took it.

keyTerms.meaning: A court's approval written on a loan document, confirming it as valid
He wrote a note planning to borrow, but never actually borrowed
Repayment of a debt
On the same day
We are not concerned (about this possibility)

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that 'people don't repay on the same day' is the key assumption. The rest of this piece attacks it.

phrases.aramaic: אִי מִשּׁוּם כָּתַב לִלְוֹת וְלֹא לָוָה –
phrases.english: If [the worry] is because he wrote [the note] to borrow but did not borrow –
look, a court approval is written in it.
phrases.notes: Only the lender would bring the note to court for approval, so the loan must have really happened.

phrases.english: If [the worry] is because of repayment –
we are not concerned about repayment on the same day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִשּׁוּם כָּתַב לִלְוֹת וְלֹא לָוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A found note with a הנפק, dated that day, is returned: the הנפק proves the loan happened, and we don't suspect same-day repayment.

steps.title: רבי זירא quotes another teaching of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks רבי אסי whether רבי יוחנן really said this. רבי אסי himself reported that רבי יוחנן said a repaid note cannot be reused for a new loan.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? Didn't you yourself say in רבי יוחנן's name: a note he borrowed with and then repaid cannot be used again to borrow, because its lien was already canceled?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins a challenge. He brings a different teaching of רבי יוחנן that seems to clash with the idea that people don't repay on the same day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new teaching talks about a note that was repaid and then reused. In the next steps רבי זירא will show that this case only makes sense if the repayment happened on the same day. That would clash with step 15.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of
He may not use it again to borrow
Was canceled or forgiven
The lien: the claim the note gives the lender on the borrower's property

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: רבי זירא said to רבי אסי:
Did רבי יוחנן really say this?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אַתְּ הוּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But isn't it you who said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
A note with which he borrowed, and then he repaid it –
he may not go back and borrow with it again,
because its lien has already been canceled.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? הָא אַתְּ הוּא דְּאָמְרַתְּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption in step 15 by bringing a different teaching of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that people do not repay a loan on the same day.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's other teaching talks about a note repaid and reused. This will be shown to mean same-day repayment.

steps.title: The case can't be a later day, because then the note would be backdated
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks when the second loan happened. If it was on a later day, רבי יוחנן should have given an easier reason: the note is backdated, and backdated notes are invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is this case? If you say the next day or some later day, why give the reason 'its lien was already canceled'? He could just say the note is backdated, and we learned in a משנה: backdated loan notes are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא is proving which case רבי יוחנן's second teaching must be about. He rules out the possibility that the second loan happened on a later day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the note was reused on a later day, its date would be earlier than the new loan. That makes it a backdated note, which is already invalid for a simple reason. Since רבי יוחנן needed the reason 'its lien was canceled', the case can't be a later day.

keyTerms.meaning: When?
If you say...
Why specifically (this reason)?
He should get it from (a simpler reason)
Backdated: dated earlier than the real loan

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying the backdating reason is wrong. He is saying that if the case were a later day, רבי יוחנן would have used that easier reason. So the case must be the same day.

phrases.english: When [is this case]?
If you say [he reborrowed] the next day or on another day,
why specifically [give the reason] 'because its lien was already canceled'?
Let him get it from the fact that it is backdated,
and we learned [in a משנה]: backdated loan notes are invalid.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in שביעית 10:5.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימַת? אִילֵּימָא לִמְחַר וּלְיוֹמָא חָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds the challenge of step 16 by working out which case רבי יוחנן's teaching must be about.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן's teaching about a repaid note cannot be about a loan taken again on a later day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה: שטרי חוב המוקדמין פסולין. On a later day the note would already be invalid as backdated, so the reason 'its lien was canceled' would not be needed.

steps.title: So people do repay on the same day
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא concludes that רבי יוחנן's teaching must be about repayment on the same day. That shows people do sometimes repay on the same day they borrowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it talking about the same day? So we see that people do repay on the same day!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא finishes his challenge. The only case left is same-day repayment, which goes against the reasoning in step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a later day is ruled out, רבי יוחנן's teaching must be about a loan repaid and reused on the same day. So רבי יוחנן himself admits that same-day repayment happens. That clashes with 'we are not concerned about same-day repayment', which was used to return the found note.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it...?
On that same day
So we see / evidently

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא shows from רבי יוחנן's own teaching that people do sometimes repay on the same day. This threatens the reason given for returning the found note.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it [talking about] the same day?
So we see that people do repay on the same day!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו בְּיוֹמֵיהּ. אַלְמָא פָּרְעִי אִינָשֵׁי בְּיוֹמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the proof in step 17 and turns it against the reasoning in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 15's claim: לפריעה בת יומא לא חיישינן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's teaching about a repaid note can only be about the same day, so he holds that people do repay on the same day. That goes against returning the found note.

steps.title: Rare, not impossible: רבי אסי clarifies his claim
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי answers רבי זירא. He never said people never repay on the same day. He only said it is uncommon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said to him: Did I say that people never repay on the same day at all? What I said is that it is not common for people to repay on the same day.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers the challenge from רבי זירא. He explains that his statement was about what is *common*, not about what is *possible*.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא proved from רבי יוחנן's other teaching that same-day repayment does sometimes happen. רבי אסי agrees with that. But something that only happens rarely is not enough of a worry to stop us from returning the note, so both teachings of רבי יוחנן can stand together.

keyTerms.meaning: they repay (a loan)
at all
common, frequent
on that same day

steps.whatToRemember: "Rare" is not the same as "never." A rare possibility is not enough to stop us from returning a lost note.

phrases.english: He said to him: Did I say
phrases.notes: This is רבי אסי answering רבי זירא.

phrases.english: that people do not repay [on the same day] at all?
That it is not common for people
to repay on that same day — that is what I said.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי קָא אָמֵינָא דְּלָא פָּרְעִי כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's conclusion in step 18 that same-day repayment does happen.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifying the claim: a statement about how often something happens, not a statement that it never happens.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא understood רבי אסי's report of רבי יוחנן to mean that same-day repayment never happens.
steps.terutzMaskana: Same-day repayment can happen but is uncommon, so we do not worry about it, and the note is returned.

steps.title: רב כהנא: the case is when the borrower admits the debt
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא offers a different explanation of רבי יוחנן. The note is returned because the borrower admits he still owes the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: רבי יוחנן's ruling is about a case where the borrower admits he owes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives another way to understand רבי יוחנן's ruling. He limits it to a case where the borrower himself says the debt was never paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this reading, we no longer need the reasoning that same-day repayment is uncommon. The borrower's own admission removes the worry that the note was already paid.

keyTerms.meaning: the one who owes, the borrower
admits

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: [It is] when the one who owes admits.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב כָּהֲנָא אָמַר: כְּשֶׁחַיָּיב מוֹדֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of רבי יוחנן's ruling (step 14), replacing the "same-day repayment is uncommon" reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן's ruling to return the note applies when the borrower admits he has not repaid.

steps.title: If the borrower admits, why say it at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא: if the borrower admits the debt, returning the note seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב כהנא. If the borrower agrees he still owes, of course we return the note, so why would רבי יוחנן need to teach this?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that רב כהנא's case makes רבי יוחנן's teaching pointless. A teaching is supposed to tell us something we would not have known by ourselves.

keyTerms.meaning: if so, if that is the case
what is there to say? (it's obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is [the point] of saying it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's explanation from step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's reading of רבי יוחנן (the borrower admits).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the borrower admits he owes, returning the note is obvious, so רבי יוחנן's teaching would add nothing.

steps.title: Why we don't suspect a trick to reuse the note
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought the borrower really paid and is only pretending he didn't, so he can reuse the note and save the scribe's fee. רבי יוחנן teaches that the lender would never go along with that, because he fears the חכמים would make him lose his money.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: this borrower really paid. He says "I didn't pay" because he wants to borrow again using this same note, and he is trying to save the scribe's fee. So רבי יוחנן teaches us: if that were so, the lender himself would not allow it. He thinks: the חכמים will hear about it and make me lose my money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why רבי יוחנן needed to teach רב כהנא's case. There was a real worry of a trick, and רבי יוחנן tells us not to worry about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A borrower's admission might be fake: he might want to reuse a paid-off note and avoid paying for a new one. But a reused paid-off note cannot be used again (step 16), and the lender knows this. He would refuse, afraid the חכמים would cancel his rights, so the borrower's admission can be trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: you might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
to borrow
the scribe's coins, the fee for writing a note
it teaches us
the lender
they will make (me) lose

steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא's case is still worth teaching: we might have suspected a fake admission, but the lender's fear of the חכמים rules that out.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a halachic rule (a paid note cannot be reused) also protects us in practice, because people avoid breaking it.

phrases.english: You might have said: this one actually repaid it,
and the fact that he says "I did not repay it"
is because he wants to go back
to borrow with it another time,
and he is worried about the scribe's coins,
so it teaches us

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִם כֵּן מַלְוֶה גּוּפֵיהּ לָא שָׁבֵק.
phrases.english: that if so, the lender himself would not allow it.

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר: שָׁמְעִי בֵּי רַבָּנַן וּמַפְסְדִי לִי.
phrases.english: He thinks: the Sages will hear and make me lose.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: הַאי מִפְרָע פַּרְעֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 by showing a real worry that רבי יוחנן's teaching rules out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן: showing that the teaching rules out a mistaken worry.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The borrower's admission might be fake, made so he can reuse a paid note and save the scribe's fee.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lender would never agree to reuse a paid note, because he fears the חכמים would make him lose his money, so the admission is trusted.

steps.title: Setting up a challenge from the משנה about found loan documents
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this case is different from the משנה that says found שטרי חוב with a property guarantee are not returned.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from what we learned in a משנה: If someone found loan documents, and they include a property guarantee, he should not return them...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge. It starts quoting an earlier משנה that seems to say the opposite of returning a found note, and the quote continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that found שטרי חוב with אחריות נכסים are not returned. That משנה was explained as a case where the borrower admits the debt, just like רב כהנא's case, yet it still says not to return the note. The גמרא is about to ask why רבי יוחנן's case should be treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference?
a property guarantee: the loan can be collected from the borrower's land
he should not return it

phrases.english: How is it different from that which we learned:
phrases.notes: This quotes a משנה from earlier in this פרק, on 12b.

phrases.english: If he found loan documents,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהֶן אַחְרָיוּת נְכָסִים – לֹא יַחֲזִיר,
phrases.english: if they include a property guarantee — he should not return [them],

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מֵהָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב כהנא's reading, the גמרא raises a contradiction from an earlier משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling to return the note, as explained by רב כהנא (the borrower admits).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says found שטרי חוב with a property guarantee are not returned, even though returning the note is what רבי יוחנן rules. The case seems similar, so why is the ruling different?

steps.title: The challenge spelled out: in the משנה the lender does go along with a misdated note
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls how the משנה about found notes was explained: the borrower admits the debt, but the note may have been written in ניסן while the loan only happened in תשרי. So the חכמים clearly did not assume the lender would insist on a new, correctly dated note.
steps.simpleTranslation: We explained that משנה as a case where the borrower admits he owes. The worry there is that the note was written to borrow in ניסן, but the loan only happened in תשרי. The lender could then wrongly seize land from people who bought from the borrower between ניסן and תשרי. So we do NOT say there that the lender himself would refuse and tell the borrower, 'Write a new note in תשרי, or the חכמים might hear and make me lose my money!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the question it started in step 23. It shows that in the משנה, the חכמים worry the lender WILL use a misdated note, while רב כהנא said the lender would never risk using a problematic note.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, רב כהנא's reasoning was that a lender fears the חכמים and would not use a questionable note. But the משנה refuses to return found notes because it worries the lender will use a note dated too early. That shows the משנה does not trust the lender's fear, which seems to contradict רב כהנא.

keyTerms.meaning: And we established (explained) the case as...
To seize or repossess property to collect a debt
Buyers who bought land from the borrower
Not according to the law, unlawfully
The lender

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is the rest of the question from step 23. The גמרא is using the משנה's case to push back against רב כהנא.

phrases.english: And we established it as a case where the debtor admits.
phrases.notes: This is the משנה about found notes from step 23.

phrases.english: And the reason is: perhaps he wrote it to borrow in Nisan
but did not actually borrow until Tishrei,
and he will come to seize land from buyers
who bought between Nisan and Tishrei, unlawfully.
And we do not say that if so,
the lender himself would not allow it,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ: כְּתוֹב שְׁטָרָא אַחֲרִינָא בְּתִשְׁרִי,
phrases.english: since he would say to him: Write another note in Tishrei,
because perhaps the Rabbis will hear and make me lose!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא אָמְרִינַן דְּאִם כֵּן מַלְוֶה גּוּפֵיהּ לָא שָׁבֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the question opened in step 23 by spelling out the משנה's case and its implication.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reasoning the גמרא gave in step 22 to defend רב כהנא's reading: that a lender would never use a questionable note out of fear of the חכמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה worries that a lender will use a misdated note, so the חכמים do not assume the lender will refuse. That contradicts רב כהנא's assumption.

steps.title: In the משנה the lender gains something; in רבי יוחנן's case he gains nothing
steps.stepSummary: The difference is profit. A misdated note lets the lender seize from more buyers, so he keeps quiet. Reusing a note whose lien was cancelled gives him no extra benefit, only risk, so he would refuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: There, in the משנה, the lender benefits, because he can seize land from buyers who bought between ניסן and תשרי. So he is happy and says nothing. Here, in רבי יוחנן's case, he gains nothing, because in the end the note only works from today. What could he seize from buyers? Nothing extra. So he would not agree to use a note whose lien was cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. A lender only takes a risk with a questionable note when it gives him an advantage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A misdated note gives the lender extra collection power over earlier buyers, so the temptation beats the fear. An old, paid-off note gives him no more power than a brand-new note would. So there is no reason to risk losing everything, and רב כהנא's reasoning stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A gain or benefit
It suits him, he is happy with it
The lien, the lender's legal claim on the borrower's land
Was forgiven or cancelled

steps.whatToRemember: A lender will risk using a questionable שטר only when it gives him a real advantage. In רבי יוחנן's case there is no advantage, so we trust that he refuses, and רב כהנא's explanation holds.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a simple rule for judging people's behavior: we expect someone to take a risk only when there is a gain.

phrases.english: They say: There,
phrases.notes: "There" means the משנה about found notes.

Here, since he has no gain,
since in the end the note counts as written now,
what is there for him to seize from buyers?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם, מִשּׁוּם דְּאִית לֵיהּ רַוְוחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 23 and 24 by showing how the two cases are different.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (benefit compared with no benefit)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that lenders ignore the fear of the חכמים, which would undercut רב כהנא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lenders ignore that fear only when they gain from it. With no gain, as in רבי יוחנן's case, the lender refuses, so רב כהנא's explanation is fine.

steps.title: New teaching: someone who claims he paid after a court action
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא quotes רבי יוחנן about a person who claims he paid after a מעשה בית דין. The ruling itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Someone who claims, after a מעשה בית דין, that he already paid...
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement begins. This line is setting up the case, and the גמרא gives the ruling at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only have the case: a person argues 'I already paid' after בית דין has acted to make him owe money. What רבי יוחנן rules about this claim comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: One who claims or argues
An action or ruling of the court
